block.heading: Long-run average cost on a diagram
block.text:
Long-run average cost (LRAC) is usually drawn as a U-shaped curve, with output on the horizontal axis and average cost on the vertical axis. A juice bottler compares factories built for monthly outputs of 10,000 to 60,000 litres. Their total costs are N$85,000, N$120,000, N$135,000, N$160,000, N$225,000 and N$360,000, so average cost is N$8.50, N$6.00, N$4.50, N$4.00, N$4.50 and N$6.00 a litre.

![LRAC curve for the juice bottler](diagrams/item-6145-5.4-031-proc-answer.png)

As the firm grows, economies of scale make average cost fall. At the lowest point, 40,000 litres at N$4.00, the firm is at its optimum size. Beyond that point diseconomies of scale outweigh economies and average cost rises. Total cost rises at every step, even from 20,000 to 40,000 litres, where average cost falls from N$6.00 to N$4.00: economies of scale are judged by cost per unit. Each point is a different factory size, so the curve does not show the short-run effect of adding workers to one factory.

item.prompt: A juice bottler compares factories, each built for one monthly output. Outputs of 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 60 thousand litres a month have total costs of N$85,000, N$120,000, N$135,000, N$160,000, N$225,000 and N$360,000. Use these data to calculate average cost and draw the long-run average cost (LRAC) curve. Label where there are economies of scale, the optimum scale and where there are diseconomies of scale, and compare the change in total cost and average cost from 20,000 to 40,000 litres (4).
item.canonical_answer: Average cost = total cost ÷ output: N$8.50, N$6.00, N$4.50, N$4.00, N$4.50 and N$6.00 a litre. Plot these against output (thousand litres a month) and join them as a U-shaped LRAC curve, with average cost (N$ per litre) on the vertical axis. Average cost falls up to 40,000 litres: economies of scale. The lowest point, N$4.00 a litre at 40,000 litres, is the optimum scale. Beyond it average cost rises: diseconomies of scale. From 20,000 to 40,000 litres total cost rises from N$120,000 to N$160,000, but average cost falls from N$6.00 to N$4.00, so it is the fall in cost per litre, not total cost, that shows economies of scale. Each point is a different factory size, so this is a long-run curve, not extra output from one factory.
